assessment:
The table prices this seat off one number and stops thinking. Eight mana in the command zone, nothing scary until then. Do not correct them.

Then go and read your own wish list, because half of it never mentions her. The enrage web runs on Dinosaurs entering, not on a commander connecting — stack 005 is the proof — so build that engine on the turns nobody is watching and let the 7/6 stay a rumour.

Learn the delivery or you will misprice every wish you cast. Worldly Tutor, Congregation at Dawn, Enlightened Tutor and Forerunner of the Empire all put the card on TOP, one draw away. You are booking an appointment, not spending a card.

Three of those four are instants, so cast them on the end step before your untap and the transit turn costs you nothing at all. Do that habitually and the reveal stops mattering.

Clock one is her arrival, and you should be buying it rather than waiting for it. She casts at a mean of turn 7.97 and shows up by turn six in only 8.3% of games, so when no reducer or cheat effect has appeared — and one shows by turn six in 56.2% of games — spend the wish there and nowhere else.

Clock two is the reveal, and it is the best exchange rate this deck offers. When she connects, every Dinosaur in the flipped cards hits the battlefield free; stack 001 turned one seven-damage swing into five bodies, three cards and a discover at six. Stack the top before combat and the flip stops being a gamble.

So stop treating a topdeck as a coin flip. Book the appointment, then keep the appointment.

targets.scenario: Turn two, end of an opponent's turn. Your hand is lands and mid-cost Dinosaurs with no acceleration in it. The table is developing quietly.
targets.why: Buy the clock before you buy anything to spend it on. One green at end of turn, draw her, cast her on turn three — her tap makes mana equal to your greatest power, so any five-power Dinosaur turns her into a rocket. This is the wish that drags a mean turn-8 commander forward by multiple turns, and the goldfish models no acceleration like her at all, so the number you are beating is already conservative.

targets.scenario: You are behind. Two opponents have wide boards of tokens and small bodies, you hold eight lands and this tutor, and your next untap is the rebuild turn.
targets.why: Take the answer nobody expects from a beatdown deck. Top it, draw it, and cast it FROM HAND — that is the trigger condition — and every non-Dinosaur creature on the battlefield dies while your board stands. A one-sided apocalypse stapled to a 7/7 beats any blocker you were considering, so stop looking for a blocker.

targets.scenario: Closing time. You have five bodies on the battlefield and you need one more haymaker to finish it.
targets.why: Ghalta costs ten less the total power of your creatures, so on the board the goldfish gives you by turn ten — a mean of 5.07 bodies — she is routinely two green mana for a 12/12 trampler. This tutor is an instant, so wish at end of turn, draw, deploy and swing on the same untap. When you are already ahead, take the cheapest twelve power in the deck.

targets.scenario: Pantlaza's discover trigger is on the stack off a five-toughness Dinosaur. You hold one green mana and this tutor. The top of your library is unknown.
targets.why: Cast the tutor in RESPONSE to the trigger and stop leaving the flip to chance. It resolves first, Regisaur Alpha goes on top, and discover five exiles it and casts it free — a 4/4, a 3/3 token and haste for the whole team, for one green mana. Control the timing and the discover stops being a lottery ticket.

tutors.notes: Every wish here is revealed, so the table sees Wakening Sun's Avatar coming a full turn out. Cast this at the last legal moment — their end step, not your main phase — and give them one turn of warning instead of two.

targets.scenario: Gishath is on the battlefield and the seat you want to attack has no profitable block. You are casting Congregation the night before the swing, or in the combat step itself.
targets.why: This is the signature play, so make it and stop hedging. Stack three Dinosaurs on top and her seven-damage reveal free-rolls all three — stack 001 is the proof of concept. Headline with Polyraptor and put Trapjaw Tyrant and Ripjaw Raptor behind it: that is the whole enrage web from stack 005 arriving in one combat step, an eight-drop and a five-drop and a four-drop for three mana and one connection.

targets.scenario: A wrath just cost you the board. You will have eight mana next turn and the table smells blood.
targets.why: Counterattack on a schedule instead of recovering on hope. Top it, draw it, hand-cast it: every non-Dinosaur creature dies and you keep a 7/7. Stack Vaultborn Tyrant second so the following draw gains you three life and replaces itself. Congregation says up to three — here you want two known cards more than you want live draws, so take two and leave it.

targets.scenario: Descendants' Path is on the battlefield, it is an opponent's end step, and your upkeep is next.
targets.why: Guarantee the reveal and take a nine-drop for free. Path reveals your top card at upkeep and casts it if it shares a type with your board — and because Path CASTS her, Zacama's untap-all-lands trigger fires, so you get a 9/9 with built-in removal and all your mana back before you have drawn for the turn. Three mana at instant speed does not buy more than that anywhere in this deck.

tutors.notes: You choose the order of the three, so choose it deliberately: card one is this turn's promise and cards two and three are your next two draws. Never stack a third card you would be unhappy to topdeck in a fire.

targets.scenario: Turn one on the play, one white source, and a hand of lands and five-drops.
targets.why: Buy the earliest mana you will ever buy. The goldfish gives you a mean 2.14 mana on turn two; Sol Ring makes it four and every turn after compounds off that. Her mean cast turn is 7.97 and every early mana point is a direct attack on that number, so cast this at end of turn one and take the discount.

targets.scenario: Mid-game, hand full of Dinosaurs, commander still in the zone. Your problem is that the whole hand is expensive, not that one card is wrong.
targets.why: Fix the hand, not the card. Name Dinosaur and every Dinosaur spell costs {2} less across a list carrying thirty-four bodies, which drops her to six mana and drops the rest of your hand with her. A reducer or cheat effect appears on its own by turn six in 56.2% of games — when it has not, this is the wish, so make it without agonising.

targets.scenario: You are behind on cards after an early skirmish. One four-power body on the battlefield, hand thinning.
targets.why: Buy the grind. It replaces itself on entry with a four-power creature out, then pays every time a big body lands — stack 001 shows a single reveal converting into three separate Uprising draws — and trample on the team turns their chump blocks back into damage. When the game goes long, keep your hand full instead of your board wide.

targets.scenario: The blue seat has held counter-mana for three straight turns and already ate your Regisaur Alpha. Your hand is stocked and your spells keep dying on the stack.
targets.why: Stop casting spells at them. Resolve the Portal naming Dinosaur and {3} plus a tap PUTS a Dinosaur from your hand onto the battlefield — no cast, nothing to counter, at instant speed on their end step. Their held mana is paper from that moment, so watch them tap out and then take your combat step.

targets.scenario: Default. Forerunner enters on turn four, the board is developing, and nothing is pointed at you yet.
targets.why: Take the web's crown jewel while the table is bored. Stack 003 verified the whole line: Forerunner pings on each Dinosaur entering, each surviving Polyraptor copies itself, and every sweep is optional — the burst caps at seven tokens and you stop the chain wherever the arithmetic peaks. That is a dial, not a gamble, so turn it exactly as far as the board wants and no further.

targets.scenario: Descendants' Path is on the battlefield and your upkeep is coming.
targets.why: Load the Path so the reveal cannot miss. Forerunner guarantees the top card is a Dinosaur, Path casts her for free, and because a Path cast is still a cast her untap-all-lands clause fires — a 9/9 with removal, life and enchantment hate at upkeep, mana refunded. Aim the Forerunner search at the Path, and let the Path do the paying.

targets.scenario: You are behind. An opponent's Voltron creature is one swing from eliminating you and your removal is spent.
targets.why: Install a turret rather than a blocker. Land it and every Forerunner ping exiles a creature an opponent controls — stack 005 puts exactly that exile on the record off one ping — so every Dinosaur you cast afterwards is a removal spell with legs. Point the first exile at the fastest clock at the table, not the biggest creature.

targets.scenario: Gishath swings unblocked next turn and Forerunner has just entered. The reveal is coming.
targets.why: Guarantee the first card she flips. Vaultborn hits the battlefield free off the reveal, gains you three, draws you a card, and its six power switches on every big-body payoff you have out — and when it dies it leaves a copy behind. The reveal was already good; spend the wish to make it certain.

tutors.notes: Forerunner is a Human Soldier running a Dinosaur company, so budget for that: the reveal never free-rolls him, the typal lands do not name him, and no Dinosaur-only search finds him. When the web is your plan, Worldly Tutor and Congregation at Dawn are the only two couriers that can go and get the hub — spend one of them on it rather than hoping.

tutors.card: Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People

targets.scenario: Huatli enters on turn three and your hand is short a white source.
targets.why: Take the colour you are actually short. White runs fourteen land sources against a thirty-six-source yardstick — the thinnest of your three, behind green's twenty and red's sixteen — and your steepest demand is Wakening Sun's Avatar at triple white, so default here and only deviate when your hand argues otherwise. Her search puts the basic in HAND, so it is a guaranteed land drop rather than a draw you might miss.

targets.scenario: You are a turn or two from casting Gishath, your board makes green and white, and red is nowhere.
targets.why: Fetch the pip the plan is missing, not the pip you already have most of. She demands red, green and white exactly, and Trumpeting Carnosaur wants double red behind her — and red sits at sixteen land sources against a thirty-six-source yardstick, so it goes missing more often than green's twenty ever does. A dead-on-colours turn eight beats a stranded turn seven every time.

targets.scenario: Roar of the Fifth People sits on chapter III at your upkeep. The blue seat has held counter-mana every turn and your last two threats died on the stack.
targets.why: Take the one they cannot touch. Chapter III puts any Dinosaur straight into your hand, and Carnage Tyrant cannot be countered and has hexproof — so cast it into their open mana and let them hold the cards. One upkeep later chapter IV hands it double strike and trample, and fourteen uncounterable damage ends the control game.

targets.scenario: Chapter III triggers with Forerunner of the Empire on the battlefield and chapter II already turning your creatures into mana.
targets.why: Close it. Chapter II's creature-mana pays the eight, Polyraptor entering hands Forerunner the dial from stack 003 — optional pings, self-copying raptors, stop where the arithmetic peaks — and chapter IV then gives every copy double strike and trample. You built the army and the kill turn off the same card, so plan the flip three upkeeps out and land chapter IV on the turn you swing.

tutors.notes: The real quest is the transformation, so pay the {3} and two hybrid at sorcery speed and start the countdown deliberately: two 3/3s, then creature-mana, then the Dinosaur wish, then double strike and trample on everything. Two upgrades on the land side while you are counting: with Wayward Swordtooth out, the basic she puts in your hand gets played the SAME turn as your normal drop, so take a Forest there — thirty-eight of your cards carry green pips and it is never wasted.

gaps: No wish here finds an instant or a sorcery, so the one-sided Blasphemous Act line — Temple Altisaur and Wrathful Raptors turning a wrath into sixteen at an opponent's face (stack 004) — can never be assembled on demand. Draw it or do not; when you draw it, protect it like the finisher it is.

Every creature wish is a delivery, not an arrival. Worldly Tutor, Congregation at Dawn and Forerunner of the Empire all put the card on TOP, one draw away, so against a table holding sweeper mana the wish can die in transit. Cast the instants at an end step and cut the exposure to zero turns; when you cannot, lean on Ripjaw Raptor and Curious Altisaur to draw you through it.

Forerunner of the Empire is the web's hub and a Human Soldier. The reveal never free-rolls him and no Dinosaur-only search reaches him, so when the web is the plan, commit Worldly Tutor or Congregation at Dawn to fetching him and do not spend both elsewhere.
Huatli's own search finds basic lands only. Treat her front face as fixing rather than as a wish, and wait for chapter III before you expect a Dinosaur out of her.
